A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaBack research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original chain-of-parities experiments, mathematical-reasoning accuracies, pass@k evaluations, and training-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional DeepScaleR results, mathematical-benchmark comparisons with R3, threshold-sensitivity experiments, and Qwen learning curves.

M1.justification: The reward-driven interval updates, partial-prefix conditioning, global-average initialization, and 10% supervision-free injection are already present in v1. v2 clarifies continuation-length notation and threshold selection without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds DeepScaleR training and evaluation, extending coverage to another, harder mathematical-reasoning dataset. The parity task, MATH, GSM8k, Base-7 GSM8k, and Tensor-2 GSM8k remain; this extends the existing domain rather than introducing a substantially different task.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates R3 only in the synthetic parity comparison. v2 Table 2 adds this closely related comparator to GSM8k, MATH, and DeepScaleR evaluations with both 1B and 3B base models, substantially strengthening the mathematical-benchmark comparison set. The original GRPO and SFT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new sensitivity experiment evaluates nine thresholds from 0.1 to 0.9 over approximately 12,000 RL iterations using SFT-initialized Llama3.2-1B on GSM8k. The new R3 comparisons explicitly share ground-truth solutions and reward functions. Previously stated GRPO batch size, rollout count, learning rate, and checkpoint aggregation are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C introduces systematic evidence about sensitivity to the central reward threshold, examining training reward, test performance, and supervision trajectories in Figures 5–6. Figure 11 adds explicit Qwen base/instruct saturation curves where v1 offered only a qualitative observation. The existing MATH saturation analysis is retained as Figure 10, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-checkpoint averaging and the same shaded pass@k curves. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval methodology, or significance tests. Its reference to inherent RL variance does not provide a new uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 values are retained. New DeepScaleR accuracies include 9.0/10.6 for AdaBack and 9.5/12.5 for SFT+AdaBack at 1B/3B. Table 2 newly shows R3 ahead on GSM8k, 41.5/74.2 versus 39.2/73.3, and slightly ahead on 3B MATH, 19.2 versus 19.1; AdaBack leads on DeepScaleR. Threshold and Qwen trajectories add further results, rather than improving previously reported scores.

T1.justification: The parity construction, sample-complexity arguments, simplifying assumptions, and Appendix B reasoning are retained. The revised continuation-length notation is a clarification; v2 introduces no substantive new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that adaptive partial supervision bridges SFT and RL, enables learning on the parity task, improves mathematical reasoning, and offers limited benefit when learning signals saturate. DeepScaleR expands supporting evidence. Although the separate pass@k contribution bullet disappears, its substantive claim remains in the experiments and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretation of the mixed R3 results: clean step segmentation may favor R3 on GSM8k, while heterogeneous difficulty and longer solutions may favor adaptive supervision. It also discusses data and compute barriers to testing longer-horizon reasoning and explains threshold robustness and the variance-based motivation for choosing 0.5. These extend the existing saturation and large-dataset limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the main threshold of 0.5, a simple boxed-answer prompt and decoding description, validation-based SFT tuning, and GRPO runs lasting at least as long as corresponding AdaBack runs. These clarify implementation and comparison practices without establishing changes to retained experiments. Hardware, token limits, and reported compute remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops its positioning against R3, replacing the earlier infeasibility characterization with discussion of fallback segmentation and conditional strengths. Section 4 and Appendix A add relationships to curriculum-versus-mixture theory, recent batch-level curricula, symbolic solvers, and stronger mathematical-reasoning pipelines. The relocated scratchpad review and duplicate Pang reference do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract opening, condenses the contribution list, revises selected experimental and R3 explanations, and changes citation style. It moves the scratchpad discussion into Appendix A and adds an LLM-usage appendix. The main section sequence and most existing technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout, expands Table 1 with DeepScaleR columns, adds Table 2 and Figures 5, 6, and 11, and substantially rearranges figure placement and sizing. v1 Figure 5 moves to appendix Figure 10; its appendix Figures 6–8 become Figures 7–9 with retained content.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves an important validation gap by comparing AdaBack directly with the closely related R3 method on mathematical benchmarks under shared solutions and rewards, including acknowledging where R3 wins. DeepScaleR and the threshold-sensitivity study further strengthen evidence for applicability and robustness while preserving the original results. These additions substantially improve empirical credibility and clarify the method's boundaries, although run-to-run uncertainty remains unquantified.
